claims.text: The browser parses the HTML it receives into the DOM, a tree of node objects (elements and text) in memory that follows the nesting of the tags; the parser also fixes up markup (e.g. closes an unclosed p, adds tbody).
claims.source_hint: MDN: Introduction to the DOM; HTML spec parsing

claims.text: The browser renders the page from the DOM (plus CSS); JavaScript can find, read, change, add and remove DOM nodes, and those changes appear on screen without loading a new page.
claims.source_hint: MDN: Introduction to the DOM; Document.querySelector; Node.appendChild

claims.text: View page source shows the HTML as the server sends it (Chrome re-requests it), not the current DOM; browser developer tools (Elements/Inspector) show and can edit the live DOM.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools / Firefox Inspector docs; MDN view-source

claims.text: Reloading a page discards the current DOM and builds a new one from the freshly received HTML.
claims.source_hint: HTML spec: navigation creates a new Document

claims.text: www/index.html has no script; html has the element children head and body; under body there are nine elements: h1, p, ul, three li and three a.
Editing an element's text in the DevTools Elements panel (double-click, type, Enter) changes the DOM and the page immediately; view source still shows the original.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools docs: Edit the DOM

claims.text: A script can register for a click on an element and, when it happens, create a new p element and insert it after the heading.
For a page with no script, like www/index.html, the DOM keeps the structure of its HTML after it is built.
claims.source_hint: reviewer r1 headless Chrome run on www/index.html

claims.text: F12 opens developer tools in most desktop browsers; the DOM view is the Elements tab (Chrome/Edge) or Inspector tab (Firefox); Ctrl+U opens view-source in a new tab in most browsers.
claims.source_hint: Chrome DevTools docs; Firefox DevTools docs

claims.text: scripts/up.sh starts the lab, and Caddy answers on http://localhost:8080 serving www/.
